review.title: CI executes every script suite the repository declares, and a failing validate job says something
review.acceptance:
CREATED ON gpt-architect's ROUND-107 DIRECTIVE. Two defects, one file.

A. EVERY SUITE THE REPOSITORY DECLARES IS EXECUTED BY CI. The validate job mirrors `npm run test:scripts` as separate named steps, and its own comment says 'a FIFTH script added to it must be added here too' -- and then records that the drift it warns about had already happened once. It has happened twice more: `test:scripts` now names SIX scripts and this job runs FOUR of them. `scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs` and `node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs` (30 cases) are in the alias and in no step. `apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` (17 cases) is in no alias and no step and is run by nothing at all.
REQUIRED: all three execute in CI and fail the build when they fail.
REQUIRED: the mirror is kept in step BY A MECHANISM, not by a comment asking a human to remember. A note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step is already in the file, it did not keep the list in step, and a fourth occurrence of the same drift is not a thing to apologise for again.
REQUIRED: the added suites run where their dependencies allow. The six pre-install steps are pre-install on purpose -- they use Node builtins only, so a dependency failure cannot mask a control-plane or structure failure -- and a suite placed there must actually hold to that.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'do not turn apps/desktop into a workspace if that causes validators to traverse generated packaging output'. Round 106 measured exactly that and it does: a dependency-free apps/desktop/package.json costs 8 lockfile lines and turbo picks the suite up, but `validate-workspace-deps.mjs` then walks apps/desktop/sidecar/server/ -- generated packaging output carrying its own .gitignore of '*' -- and demands the manifest declare `next`. The measurement is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.

B. A FAILING `validate` JOB SAYS SOMETHING ACTIONABLE. On run 37028642916 at 30cef6e the job aborted at 10m 38s with one annotation, 'Process completed with exit code 134', naming no step -- having PASSED at 25m 4s and 27m 29s on the two runs before it. Exit 134 is SIGABRT. The engineering session cannot read run logs or download artifacts (the Actions API answers 403) and so could not determine which step aborted, let alone why; two local reproductions of the prime suspect passed, at 1261s ambient and 1807s under a runner-like heap cap.
REQUIRED: a run page carries enough to tell a reader WHICH step aborted and under what machine conditions -- at minimum core count, total and available memory, free disk, the Node version and NODE_OPTIONS -- without needing the log or the artifact.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'DO NOT declare OOM. DO NOT increase memory merely because exit 134 occurred. DO NOT increase timeouts without evidence. DO NOT add retries to hide it. Improve diagnostics first.' Nothing in this task may change what CI runs or how much it is given. Diagnostics only.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: no secret leakage. Nothing added here may print the environment wholesale, a token, or a value this repository has not already published; an allowlist of named variables, never a dump.

C. THE JOB'S COST DOES NOT GROW MATERIALLY. The three added suites take under a second between them locally. Diagnostics must stay cheap enough that nobody is tempted to remove them the next time the job is slow.

unit.evidence:
RE-RECORDED AFTER THE SECOND REPAIR THIS ROUND. Both repairs stand together; the evidence below replaces nothing in the previous recording and adds what the second one needed.

REPAIR 1 (from CI #178): scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs moved from the pre-install group to immediately after `Install dependencies`. It was placed pre-install on the strength of its IMPORTS -- builtins and git -- and four of its nine cases SPAWN a real `next dev`, which is in node_modules. Reproduced in a fresh clone of 975331c with no node_modules: 5 passed, 4 failed, the suite's own non-vacuity guard naming it. After the move, with node_modules present, "desktop-target tests passed (9 assertions)". The comment in the file records the rule the mistake broke: the pre-install group is about what a suite RUNS, not what it imports.

REPAIR 2 (found by me, after returning the first): THE DIAGNOSTICS WERE WRITTEN SOMEWHERE THIS SESSION CANNOT READ. Round 107 justified writing them to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY on the claim that a summary "renders on the run page". It does not. On 975331c two workflows wrote summaries -- this one and windows.yml's lifecycle report -- and neither is reachable: runs 37094053423 and 37094053371 were each fetched at both the run page and the job page, and the only "Summary" visible is GitHub's own metadata and artifact list. Not one word the workflow wrote. Clause 4 of the verdict -- "the run page now exposes actionable diagnostic information" -- was therefore NOT met by the version returned an hour ago.

WHAT IS DEMONSTRABLY READABLE IS AN ANNOTATION, and every CI fact this project has obtained came from one. So the three facts that matter are now emitted as workflow commands as well, with the summary kept for a human reading in a browser:
  ::warning "validate failed"    -- the first failing step, derived from the step ids;
  ::notice  "validate machine"   -- cores, memory, free disk, node, npm and NODE_OPTIONS, BEFORE and AFTER on one line, which is what makes either number mean anything;
  ::warning "V8 fatal error"     -- the redactor's new --line mode, same allowlist rendered on one line.

EXECUTED UNDER GITHUB'S OWN SHELL FLAGS (bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail), three branches, each exit 0:
  - with a V8 report present: all three annotations emitted, the V8 one carrying event, trigger, heap limit/committed/used, external, rss, peak rss, free and total memory, cpu seconds and the entry script;
  - with no report and no facts file: the machine annotation says "BEFORE not recorded" rather than failing, and no V8 annotation is emitted;
  - runner-facts writes its file and its summary, exit 0.
THE ALLOWLIST STILL HOLDS ON THE NEW PATH, tested as an attack: a process aborted with SECRET_TOKEN=hunter2 in its environment leaves the value once in the raw diagnostic report and ZERO times in the emitted annotation. The raw report is still never printed and never uploaded.

ANNOTATIONS ARE KEPT FEW AND SHORT -- three, each truncated at 380 characters -- because they are capped and truncated by GitHub, and a verdict cut in half is worse than a short one. The step-by-step table stays in the summary where length is free.

AND THE CORRECTION THAT WEAKENS THIS TASK'S ORIGINAL JUSTIFICATION, repeated here because it belongs with the evidence: rounds 106 and 107 said the annotation "names an exit code and no step". It names the step -- on the JOB page, which needs no login; the RUN page drops the attribution, and that is the page both rounds read. Run 37036128012's validate job says exit 134 under "Test AI control plane". The comment in ci.yml asserting the limitation is corrected in the file, and what the step-outcome table is still worth is stated narrowly there: it separates a step that FAILED from one that never STARTED, and it survives a job that ends with no annotation at all.

LOCAL RE-VERIFICATION: ci.yml parses, 20 steps; the mirror check passes against the repaired file; the moved suite passes where it now runs.

review.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
review.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.
review.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

build.evidence: npm run build (turbo) at 95d8b7658065b4c52699d6e0882ed7d04a119a21: Tasks 12 successful, 12 total, exit 0. STATED PLAINLY: 11 of 12 were cache hits, because this task's surface is apps/desktop/scripts, docs/LICENSING.md and a coordination document, and none of that is a build input for any workspace. A build gate on a change the build graph cannot see is close to vacuous and saying otherwise would be a green mark that means nothing. WHAT ACTUALLY EXERCISES THIS ROUND'S CODE: node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs, 17 cases, 0 failures, covering the three historical shapes of a manifest licence field, the four evidence verdicts, the filename pattern, and the rendered document's ordering, timestamp-freedom, escaping and written-offer text. collect-notices.mjs exercised end to end against a synthetic packaged tree: scoped packages, the legacy { type } manifest shape, a LICENSE-MIT file, a package with no evidence at all, and --strict exiting 1. The runtime-licence copy verified BOTH WAYS -- the generated notices carry 'No LICENSE accompanied this binary' when none is present and do not when one is. node --check on package-sidecar.mjs, collect-notices.mjs, notices.mjs and notices.test.mjs. Also clean at the same commit: npm run lint 12/12 with 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in PW-0313's surface), npm run repo:validate, npm run ai:validate (114 tasks). THE TEST FOUND A REAL BUG IN THE FIRST ATTEMPT: the licence-filename pattern allowed only an extension, so a dual-licensed package shipping LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE would have been reported as carrying no licence text at all. UNVERIFIED AND NOT CLAIMED: no libmpv or FFmpeg build was produced -- this container's toolchains target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- and the notices generator has never run against a real packaged tree, because packaging happens on Windows. What the real dependency list will say is a thing the first Windows packaging run prints and nobody here can predict.

review.title: Series navigation and the next episode
review.acceptance: A viewer can move through a series without going back to the catalog. Today every season of a series renders as one flat stack on the title page, with no season selector, no per-episode progress and no way to reach the next episode. REQUIRED: season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place. REQUIRED: per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API. REQUIRED: a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place. REQUIRED: the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a component, because 'what plays next' is exactly the kind of decision this project requires to be reconstructible.
review.notes:
PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. 

ROUND 109 SURFACE AMENDMENT, recorded as an event before any write: player-surface.tsx and app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx move from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths, and three new components/title/next-episode-prompt.* files are named. The last unmet clause is the affordance AT THE END OF PLAYBACK, which only the player can know about and only the server can gate. PW-0306 owned player-surface.tsx and is DONE as of this round, so the surface is free. components/player/controls/** was deliberately NOT taken: the prompt is not a control and the controls must not learn what a series is.

unit.evidence:
npm run test: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. apps/web 1614 tests passed, up from 1597 -- 17 new, 0 failed.

THE LAST CLAUSE, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ROUND ADDED: "a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place."

THE GATE IS THE SAME GATE AND IS NEVER RESTATED. The chain is one line of imports: the watch page calls nextUpFor, which calls resolveNextEpisode, which calls resolvePlayAvailability -- the function episode-list.tsx applies to every row. The href the client receives is the one that function returned. There is no string concatenation anywhere on the path.

AND THAT IS CHECKED MECHANICALLY RATHER THAN BY INTENTION, in two places, because a mutation proved an assertion about VALUES cannot do it. Replacing `href: next.href` with a template literal building `/watch/${id}` PASSED ALL TWENTY behavioural tests -- and it has to, since resolvePlayAvailability builds exactly that string, so the honest answer and the forged one are identical for every episode a fixture can describe. The difference is only visible in the source. Both next-episode.ts and next-episode-prompt.tsx are now parsed with their comments stripped and asserted to contain no "/watch" literal and no watchHref call. With that guard in place the mutation fails.

17 NEW TESTS.
  next-episode.test.ts, 6 new (20 -> 21 including the source guard): the projection carries the gate's own href; it counts refused episodes instead of naming them; it answers null for all three absences, which is one screen and not a taxonomy; it carries no rights basis, synopsis or artwork across the server/client boundary; and the source guard above.
  next-episode-prompt.test.tsx, 11 new: what it says, what it refuses to say about WHY episodes were skipped, the address, that it is a link and not a button, that it is a named region and NOT an alert, and two source-level guards -- no path construction, and no setTimeout/setInterval/router.push, because the acceptance forbids an autoplay and this component autoplays nothing at all.

MUTATION-TESTED: three mutations on the projection, two caught behaviourally (always-zero skip count; returning a projection when the gate refused everything) and the third -- building the href -- only caught after the source guard was added, which is why the guard exists.

NOTHING IN THE EXISTING CLAUSES MOVED. Season navigation, the episodeCount invariant that throws at import, per-episode progress and the pure next-episode rule are untouched; their tests are among the 1614.

e2e.evidence:
Development, full chromium+api suite: 108 passed / 15 skipped / 0 failed, up from 103 passed -- the five new cases are the end-of-playback clause. Production + real PostgreSQL 16, cold database, --workers=4: 77 passed / 46 skipped / 0 failed; the five skip there with their reason named, because /watch refuses before a player exists on a build with no catalog source.

HOW THE END OF PLAYBACK IS REACHED IN A BROWSER, AND EXACTLY WHAT IS SIMULATED. No real media decodes in this harness -- the demo catalog's sources are fixtures -- so nothing can play a programme to its end. What the test dispatches is the `ended` EVENT ON THE REAL <liberty-video> ELEMENT, which is the event a real ending fires. Everything downstream is the product and none of it is stubbed: WebPlayerAdapter's own listener, its `ended` adapter event, the machine's MEDIA_ENDED, the transition into the `ended` phase, and player-surface rendering from that phase. THE ONLY THING FAKED IS THE DECODER. It is dispatched rather than the `ended` property being assigned, because the element's listeners are what the adapter attached to and a property would prove nothing about the wiring.

THE FIVE CASES.
  NOTHING IS OFFERED UNTIL THE PROGRAMME ENDS -- and the prompt is asserted absent from the DOCUMENT, not merely invisible. A hidden affordance is still in the accessibility tree, and a screen reader that can find "Next episode" mid-programme has been told the ending early.
  When it ends, S1 E2 is offered AND ONLY OFFERED: the URL is still the episode the viewer was watching. Nothing counts down and nothing navigates.
  The offer is a LINK with the accessible name "Play S1 E2" -- not "Play", which is what a screen-reader user meets out of context -- it is focusable, Enter follows it, and it lands on /watch/<next>, the ORDINARY route with the ordinary session request and the ordinary authorization decision. No bespoke play-next path.
  AT THE END OF THE SERIES, NOTHING IS OFFERED AND NOTHING WRAPS AROUND. A player that wrapped to S1 E1 would fail the deterministic-end clause in the most confusing possible way.
  A FILM OFFERS NOTHING, because "next" is a question about a series.

MUTATION-TESTED IN THE BROWSER, NOT ONLY IN UNIT TESTS. Rendering the prompt regardless of the machine phase: 1 failed. Dropping nextUp on the watch page: 2 failed. Both reverted.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The ending was dispatched, not decoded. The rights gate's refusal path at this affordance -- an episode whose basis lapses between the page render and the click -- is not exercised here and cannot be: the gate runs on the server at render time, and /watch/:id re-decides on arrival, which is the arrangement that makes the stale case safe rather than a case this spec can stage.
